html:
The great law code of Joseon Korea, finished in its final form in 1485 under King Seongjong. It laid out how the kingdom was governed and stayed the base of its law for about four hundred years.

King Sejo ordered it in 1458 to replace a patchwork of earlier codes from the dynasty's founding. A full draft was ready by 1467, but revisions went on until the 1485 version was issued.

It is arranged in six parts, matching the six ministries of the state: personnel, revenue, rites, war, punishments and works. It covered the ranks and duties of officials, taxes and land, the civil service exams, family law and inheritance, the army, crimes and public works.

The code put Neo-Confucian ideas into law. It fixed a social order led by the scholar class, the yangban. Later kings added supplements rather than replacing it, until the Gabo Reform of the 1890s swept much of the old order away. Its model was the Chinese tradition of codes, such as the Great Ming Code.
sum: The great law code of Joseon Korea, finished in its final form in 1485 under King Seongjong. It laid out how the kingdom was governed and stayed the base of its law for about four hundred years.
